The door swings shut behind you, and the chill of the courtyard is gone. Firelight plays across old timbers. Somewhere a lute is being played, not quite in tune, and nobody seems to mind.
Every table is taken. Fighters compare scars while a young mage pretends not to listen. In the gallery above, a priest blesses a bowl of stew, and the thief beside him quietly counts the spoons.
Behind the bar stands a broad, gray-bearded man with his arms folded and a smile that has outlasted a great many customers.
"Welcome, welcome," says
Gilgamesh

. "Another one answering Trebor's call, I see. Sit anywhere you like. Not that table, though. It's kept for a party that went down to settle matters with Werdna." He polishes a tankard thoughtfully. "Some while ago now."
He nods toward the crowded room.

"Everyone here means to go down into the Maze, and the wise ones know better than to go alone. Choose your companions with care. A friend who will carry you home is worth more than gold. A friend who offers to carry your gold is not quite the same thing."
You notice that good and evil seldom share a table for long. Gilgamesh assures you they fare even worse sharing a corridor beneath the castle.
"Well, then," says Gilgamesh, setting down the tankard. "Find yourself some good company. The Maze will still be there in the morning. It always is."

items.text: Your adventure begins with good company. Gather your party.

text.text: The heavy oak door closes behind you, shutting out the noise of the castle courtyard. Warmth, candlelight, and the comforting smell of fresh bread greet you. Across the hall, a fire crackles, and the distant sound of laughter drifts down a corridor.
Behind a polished wooden desk stands a smiling woman in a blue-and-gold gown. An enormous ledger lies open before her, beside a brass bell and a quill and inkwell.
"Welcome to the Adventurer's Inn," she says. "I'm
Mistress Elspeth
. You look as though you've come from the Maze. Or are about to. It's sometimes difficult to tell."
She glances at your companions with a practiced eye.

"Stables are free, of course. A little straw, a roof overhead, and time enough to recover your spells. But if you've acquired a few injuries, I recommend a proper bed. We have accommodations for every purse, from a modest cot to the Royal Suite."
She pauses, turning a page in her ledger.
"Naturally, the better the room, the quicker the recovery. Gold has a remarkable effect on one's health, I've found."
Her smile softens.
"And should one of your companions be in a condition that sleep cannot remedy, I'm afraid you'll need the Temple of Cant. We provide beds, not miracles."
She reaches for her quill.
"Now then, who's staying, and how long?"

items.text: Rest your adventurers, restore their spells, and heal their wounds. Choose your accommodations carefully; comfort has its price.

text.text: The door opens with the cheerful jingle of a brass bell. Warm light spills across polished armour, racks of swords, and shelves crowded with bottles of suspiciously brilliant colours. Somewhere beneath the counter, a cat opens one eye, judges you unworthy of further attention, and goes back to sleep.
Behind a great wooden counter sits a round, white-haired gentleman whose smile grows noticeably wider as he notices your purse.
"Welcome, welcome!" cries
Boltac
, spreading his arms. "The finest weapons, the stoutest armour, the most remarkable magical treasures in all of Trebor's kingdom! And every one of them reasonably priced!"
You glance at a battered shield bearing what looks remarkably like a fresh dragon bite.
"Previously owned," Boltac explains smoothly. "By a gentleman who no longer requires it. Excellent workmanship."
He gestures toward his shelves.
"Buy, sell, identify, remove a troublesome curse — all under one roof! Though I should mention that certain enchantments are rather more difficult to remove than they are to acquire."
He leans forward confidentially.
"Now, should you happen to discover anything interesting in Werdna's Maze, bring it straight to me. I pay a fair price for everything. Well, almost everything."
The cat raises its head at the sound of coins being counted.
Boltac smiles again.
"Remember, my friend: a good sword may save your life. A better sword may save it twice. And if neither does, I'll be delighted to purchase them back from whoever brings them home."

items.text: Equip your adventurers, inspect unfamiliar treasures, and spend your gold wisely. Boltac never forgets a customer — particularly one who still owes him money.

text.text: Where darkness meets the promise of light
The great doors close behind you with a deep, hollow echo.
Within the ancient Temple of Cant, towering columns of dark stone rise into vaulted ceilings lost in shadow. The air is cool and still, heavy with the fragrance of incense.
High above the altar, magnificent stained-glass windows depict the eternal passage between life and death. A hooded figure descends into darkness, while another rises toward a brilliant light.
A slender ribbon of incense smoke curls upward from a suspended bronze censer. As it passes through a shaft of violet light, it shimmers for a moment before disappearing into the shadows.

Beside a stone bier stands a tall elven priest, his long silver hair falling over robes of charcoal and silver. His angular features and high cheekbones speak of an ancient lineage, while his expression carries the quiet sorrow of one who has witnessed countless departures.
Father Caelion, Keeper of the Veil.
He turns toward you, resting one hand upon his ceremonial staff.
"Welcome, Commander, to the Temple of Cant."
His voice is gentle, yet carries effortlessly through the great sanctuary.
"Here we tend those whom the darkness has touched. Petrification may be reversed, paralysis lifted, and even death itself may sometimes be persuaded to release its hold."
He gestures toward the stone bier.
"Many have rested upon that stone. Some have risen again to walk beneath the sun. Others have passed beyond our reach."
His eyes turn toward the great stained-glass window.
"Understand this, Commander. We are servants of Cant, not masters of life and death. We may petition for mercy, but we cannot command it."
For a moment, the sanctuary falls silent.
"Even the most faithful prayer may fail. And each attempt to recall a departed soul carries its own peril. What was once flesh may become ashes, and what has become ashes may yet be lost forever."
He looks back at you.
"Bring me your wounded and your fallen. We shall do all that is within our power."
A faint, knowing smile crosses his face.
"And as for the offerings required by the Temple..."
He pauses, glancing toward a discreetly placed collection chest.
"Even those who serve eternity must attend to the expenses of the present."
The incense continues its slow ascent toward the light.
"Now, Commander. Whom have you brought before Cant?"
The maze.
The party sets out from here.
Beyond the walls of Trebor's castle

The sound of clashing steel carries across the dusty training grounds. Beneath the castle's towering battlements, recruits of every race practice their trades. Swords strike wooden targets, arrows whistle through the air, and a young mage struggles to control a flame dancing between her fingers.
Overseeing this confusion stands a broad-shouldered dwarf with an iron-grey beard, an immaculate uniform, and a magnificent double-headed battle axe resting casually across one shoulder.
Sergeant Major Brannock Ironheel.

Veteran of more campaigns than anyone cares to remember, Brannock has trained generations of adventurers for the service of Trebor. His medals are polished, his boots immaculate, and his patience legendary for its absence.
"So, you're the new commander, eh? Well, I've got fighters, priests, thieves, and mages for you to look over. Some promising specimens among 'em. Some I'd hesitate to trust with a spoon."
"You choose 'em, Commander. I'll see they're properly prepared. But remember, a fine-looking recruit doesn't necessarily make a fine adventurer."
He shifts his enormous double-headed axe.
"Once you've selected your people, take 'em to Gilgamesh. He'll help you assemble your party. After that, what happens underground is your responsibility."
He pauses, then adds:
"And Commander? Try to bring 'em back. I hate training replacements."

text.text: You have arrived at the Castle of Trebor, the Mad Overlord, whose lands lie beneath the shadow of a terrible evil.
Deep below the Castle, the wizard Werdna has hidden himself within a vast and treacherous Maze. There he guards a powerful amulet stolen from Trebor himself.
The Overlord has called upon adventurers from every corner of the realm. Riches and glory await those brave enough to descend into the labyrinth, defeat Werdna, and return with the stolen amulet.
Many have answered the call. Few have returned.
Now it is your turn.
But no adventurer should face the Maze alone. You must first gather a company of companions, each bringing their own strengths, skills and knowledge of magic.
Your journey begins at the Edge of Town.
There you may establish a new adventure and visit the Training Grounds, where warriors, priests, mages and thieves begin their journeys.

Create your characters, choosing their names, races, professions and abilities. Then return to the Castle, where Gilgamesh's Tavern provides a gathering place for your party, Boltac's Trading Post offers equipment, and the Adventurer's Inn provides rest.
When your company is assembled and prepared, the Maze awaits.
